1.1.evaluator_rationale: The candidate sentences discuss violence against women and children generally (including within the family/household) and list forms of violence, but they do not explicitly mention or define “domestic violence” as a specific category.

evidence_candidates.text:
Article 29
(1) Regional Apparatus with authority over Women and Children shall formulate service policy regarding the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
(2) The formulation of service policy as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented through the following mechanism:
a. formulating case reporting policy related to Women and Children who become Victims of acts of Violence;
b. preparing reporting and referral mechanisms between regional apparatus organizations with authority over the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence with relevant agencies and with P2TP2A; and
c. preparing budget for the implementation of protection policy for Women and Children against acts of Violence.

Part Eleven
Child-Friendly Regency Development Policy

Article 17
The obligations of the Family and/or parents as referred to in Article 13 letters c and d have full responsibility to prevent all forms of Violence and protect Women and Children as members of the Family.

CHAPTER V
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

Article 11
Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e is caused by: a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the Victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or Services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the Victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

1.1.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, “domestic violence” is explicitly covered within the definition of violence: Pasal 1 angka 5 defines Kekerasan as acts causing suffering “dan/atau penelantaran rumah tangga” (and/or household/domestic neglect), and Pasal 10(c) also refers to neglect “orang dalam lingkup Rumah Tangganya” (persons within the household). This is the policy’s way of addressing violence in the domestic/household sphere (KDRT-related), even if it does not create a separate labeled category called “domestic violence.” However, the retrieved candidates shown to the judge did not include Pasal 1(5) or Pasal 10, so the judge lacked the key evidence needed to answer Yes. The judge’s ‘No’ is therefore mainly due to retrieval not surfacing the relevant passages.

1.6.evaluator_rationale: None of the candidate sentences explicitly mention harmful practices such as child/early marriage, female genital mutilation, honour crimes, or female infanticide.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is South Labuhanbatu Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of South Labuhanbatu.
4. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion either directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
5. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a Child who is still in the womb.
7. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
8. Violence against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against Children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of Children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences violence and/or threat of violence.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from acts of Violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
15. Gender is the difference in characteristics, roles, functions and status between Women and men which is not based on biological differences, but rather based on socio-cultural relations influenced by the broader structure of society.
16. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate Gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region.
17. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as Dinas PPPA is the office that administers the affairs of Women's empowerment and Child Protection.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women's and Children's Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated Service center in the effort to empower Women and Children established by the Regional Government with active Community participation which includes an information center, consultation center, complaint service, initial health care, counseling, legal assistance, repatriation and social reintegration, shelter/temporary safe house (shelter), as well as a referral center.
19. Safe House is a shelter/temporary protection house for Victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of Victims from threats and danger from perpetrators, and is only known by relevant parties such as certain personnel at UPT P2TP2A for reasons of Victim safety and security.
20. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is the standard steps that must be taken in protecting Victims starting from complaints/identification, rehabilitation, health, Social Rehabilitation, advocacy up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or Victims.
21. Family is the smallest unit in Society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child or Family by blood in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree and/or if any up to the fourth degree.
22. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have Family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, representation, and/or Household workers and reside in that Household.
23. Community is individuals, Families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
24. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of South Labuhanbatu Regency.
25. Social Rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out their social functions properly in Community life.

1.6.rationale: Reviewing the original Indonesian regulation, it does not appear to include ‘harmful practices’ as typically defined in this indicator (e.g., child/early marriage, FGM, honour crimes, female infanticide). The closest relevant mention is Pasal 38 huruf b: “mencegah terjadinya perkawinan pada usia anak-anak” (prevent child-age marriage). That is a harmful practice (child marriage) and would support a Yes if the indicator counts child marriage prevention as coverage. However, the retrieved candidates shown to the judge did not include Pasal 38 at all, and the judge correctly noted the absence of explicit harmful-practice mentions in the provided English passages. Given the discrepancy setup (golden=Yes), the more fundamental problem is that the golden label likely relied on Pasal 38(b), but the evaluation packet omitted it; if the golden label expects explicit harmful practices, it is only supported by that single child-marriage-prevention clause. Because the judge had no access to Pasal 38, the disagreement is best attributed to a golden-labeling expectation mismatch (golden assumes coverage) rather than judge error; the golden label should be reconsidered or clarified to ensure Pasal 38(b) is within scope and retrievable.
